contributions.body: source-1 — Complete independent source contribution after reading all 1,251 lines of my frozen production brief. Mechanism: the Karime overlay names a small buyer hesitation and the agent answers at the scale of the decision. The caption then ACTS like that helpful agent through recognizable things the buyer can do; warmth is carried by the conversation rather than announced. That causal explanation is an editorial hypothesis; mixed recognition comments and public attention support resonance, not conversion. What changes here: the buyer’s problem is evaluating a home against an ordinary need (quiet movie time) while liking the condo’s finish and seeing work in the detached alternative. Do not merely replace 'question' with 'noise' in a permission post. The new conversation must move the decision forward: allow the buyer to keep liking a place AND take the noise concern seriously, without being hurried into either dismissing the concern or discarding every condo. Source supports uncertainty about future neighbors; it does not establish that the candidate condo is already noisy. The crucial distinction is concern to investigate versus confirmed defect. Jen should neither promise quiet nor announce a property-type verdict. A particularly tempting but unsupported line would assert 'you can hear their TV through the wall' at the candidate. Source-grounded texture: quiet movie watching is the goal; existing neighbor noise is what the buyer wants to leave; detached-home work is a real competing burden. Use these as an illustrative reader situation, never 'my buyer told me' or Jen's own lived experience. Neighborhood span is grounding for us, not compulsory name-dropping in copy. Avoid copying the source buyer’s years of arguments in a way that reads like a borrowed client story. Desired reader effect: 'She understands why this matters, and I can tell her what is bothering me without getting pushed into a home-type argument.' No added CTA required; any invitation should advance this precise conversation. Production: ordinary footage, no sound demonstration, no staged neighbor confrontation, no promised sound test or property inspection result. Please acknowledge source-1 with ONE exact craft decision that changes or is explicitly preserved because of this contribution. I have not read a draft or contacted the solo route.

# craft-1 — locked initial team draft

## On-screen text

“the condo is so much nicer.
i just don’t want to hear
my neighbors again.”

you don’t have to talk yourself
out of wanting a quiet home.

## Full caption

you can already picture your couch in the condo. the kitchen is done. you wouldn’t have to spend your weekends fixing things before it feels like home.

and then you remember the neighbors where you live now and start negotiating with yourself. maybe it wouldn’t bother me as much here. maybe i’m being too picky.

you can love the condo and still be unsure about living there. i’m not going to point at the countertops until you forget what was bothering you 😂

especially when the other place you’re considering is a house that needs work, and you really weren’t hoping to come home to another project.

i can’t tell you a place will be quiet just because it doesn’t share a wall. we don’t have to pretend either option is an easy yes.

but if getting home and being able to unwind is a big part of why you’re moving, i want that in the conversation while we’re looking. even if the kitchen is giving you very good reasons to change the subject.

tell me what you’re hoping you won’t have to deal with in the next place. “i want to sit on my couch and relax” is plenty to work with.

## Ordinary existing-footage direction

Jen can choose an existing relaxed clip of herself walking through a room or standing in a property, with room around her for the text. One ordinary clip is enough. Show the buyer thought first, then replace it with the complete reply; give each a comfortable reading hold. No acting out the conversation, new filming, spoken script, noise effects, or neighboring-property comparison. This is footage direction only; no available clip has been selected or inspected here.

## Cover treatment

Text: “i just want some quiet”

Use a clear still from Jen’s chosen clip, with the line in her existing cover treatment, readable at grid size and clear of her face. Jen chooses the footage and cover; this does not claim a rendered asset.

## Source-to-adaptation note

The external Reel contributes relaxed property B-roll, a recognizable buyer concern followed by an agent response, and a caption that continues the relationship through ordinary language. The new situation comes from one self-reported SFV buyer weighing a better-finished condo against a house needing work while wanting relief from current neighbor noise. This changes the conversation from asking another question to allowing daily comfort to affect the decision; the candidate condo’s noise remains unknown. The language follows the approved Jen caption’s directness, small humor and fuller conversational turns. The reference has observed public attention and mixed recognition comments; it is not a verified creator-relative outlier or conversion proof. New writing remains an adaptation hypothesis pending Farrice’s comparison.

# editor-1 — complete peer review

Full craft-1 reviewed against the complete frozen packet. Timing: your draft arrived before I sent editor-initial, so that diagnostic was not preregistered. My main challenge is the last third: it explains Jen's stance twice, then asks for a general disclosure. The approved caption stays inside a believable exchange; this one begins to summarize its purpose.

## Retain

- “you can already picture your couch in the condo. the kitchen is done.” The couch gives the attraction a recognizable image; the kitchen detail stays within the finished-interior premise.
- “i’m not going to point at the countertops until you forget what was bothering you 😂” This is the most Jen-like moment: a small joke about what she will actually do, not a claim about empathy or an invented past client.
- The house needing work must remain explicit, once. It makes the uncertainty particular; removing it would turn this into a generic noisy-neighbors reassurance post.
- The honest distinction that a detached house does not guarantee quiet. It can stay as one conversational sentence, without the second balancing sentence.

## Change

1. “you wouldn’t have to spend your weekends fixing things before it feels like home.” This implies an unverified repair-free condition, and the weekend/home-feeling consequence is invented. Suggested replacement connecting the known alternatives: “then you look at the house that needs work and go back to the condo pictures.” It describes an illustrative decision loop, not a property-condition assurance. If used, delete the later paragraph beginning “especially when the other place...” to avoid explaining the same tradeoff twice.
2. “maybe it wouldn’t bother me as much here.” The pronoun makes candidate-condo noise sound established. Replace with: “maybe it’ll be different this time. maybe i’m being too picky.” This preserves the buyer's uncertainty and self-minimizing turn.
3. “i can’t tell you a place will be quiet just because it doesn’t share a wall. we don’t have to pretend either option is an easy yes.” Keep the first sentence or use “and a house with no shared walls doesn’t automatically answer that for you.” Drop the second: it restates ambiguity in a neat editorial summation.
4. The paragraph beginning “but if getting home and being able to unwind...” explains the content's purpose and repeats the kitchen joke. Try a concrete continuation instead: “if you’re standing in a showing thinking, please let me be able to come home and relax here, tell me that. even if you were just saying how much you loved the kitchen.” This remains an illustrative thought, and connects attraction to the unspoken need without promising a property answer.

## Closing challenge

“tell me what you’re hoping you won’t have to deal with in the next place” is a useful question, but with the paragraph before it the ending asks for the same disclosure twice. Choose one actual line Jen could say to this buyer. If you adopt replacement 4, drop the current closing paragraph; that proposed paragraph can close the caption without a second prompt. If you keep your original final couch line, shorten the preceding paragraph substantially and drop its second kitchen joke.

## Overlay / format / evidence

The overlay's concern→response works, and its use of an illustrative buyer thought is explicitly allowed. “talk yourself out of wanting a quiet home” is more polished than the approved exchange but understandable; don't add an extra lesson to explain it. Existing-footage direction and cover treatment fit the assignment and honestly preserve unselected/unrendered status. Source-to-adaptation note correctly separates public attention, unknown condo noise and unproven preference/conversion. No new factual research is needed for these edits. These are editorial recommendations, not approval.
